newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were expected to open lower Friday on overnight fund liquidation and producer hedge selling on a stronger dollor, dealers said.
COMEX December gold was called $0.50 to $1.00 lower from its previous close of $328.00 an ounce after trading from $327.00 to $327.90 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $323.25/3.75 early against the London morning fix of $323.50.
COMEX warehouse gold and silver stocks were unchanged at 946,079 ounces and 165,395,967 ounces, respectively, in Thursday's data.
The stronger dollar brought up the value of gold in other currencies, dealers said, prompting long liquidation and producer selling in dollar-denominated contracts.

Thursday's New York market sustained losses on U.S. consumer price index data that came in at 0.2 percent as expected plus a stock market the staved off losses after a 4.9 percent loss in the S&P500 index earlier this week.
COMEX September silver was called to open down 1.00-2.00 cents from Thursday's close of $4.405 an ounce.

NYMEX October platinum was expected to open $4.00-$5.00 lower from Thursday's close at $427.80 an ounce, while NYMEX September palladium was seen opening up $1.00 an ounce from the previous close at $209.85 an ounce.
